title: Broken Access Control
description: Asgard is the final realm demonstrating complex broken access control through a multi-stage exploit chain: IDOR → Blind SQL Injection → SSRF → Metadata Service Access.
theme: Norse realm of gods - the ultimate challenge requiring mastery of all techniques

endpoints.description: Employee details with insufficient authorization checks

vulnerabilities.description: Phase 1: The employee details endpoint lacks proper authorization checks. Users can access other employees' information by enumerating ID parameters, revealing admin email addresses needed for subsequent exploits.
vulnerabilities.impact: Information disclosure, access to admin details, enables further exploit chain
exploit_indicators: Access to employee IDs outside user's authorization
Response contains email addresses and roles
vulnerabilities.remediation: Implement proper authorization checks. Validate user permissions before returning resources. Use indirect references (UUIDs). Implement access control lists (ACLs). Log and monitor IDOR attempts.

vulnerabilities.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command

endpoints.description: Password reset with blind SQLi vulnerability

vulnerabilities.description: Phase 2: The password reset endpoint is vulnerable to blind SQL injection. Using the admin email from IDOR, attackers can extract the password reset token through boolean-based blind SQLi.
vulnerabilities.impact: Account takeover, admin access, enables SSRF exploitation
exploit_indicators: SQL boolean operators in email parameter (AND, OR)
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use parameterized queries exclusively. Implement input validation. Use ORM frameworks. Apply WAF rules. Monitor for SQLi patterns.

vulnerabilities.type: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via CRLF Injection

endpoints.description: Report viewer vulnerable to SSRF via header injection

vulnerabilities.description: Phase 3: Using admin access, the report viewer endpoint can be exploited with CRLF injection to bypass SSRF filters and access internal metadata services containing the flag.
vulnerabilities.impact: Access to internal services, credential theft, flag retrieval, potential RCE
vulnerabilities.remediation: Sanitize CRLF characters. Validate and encode all URL inputs. Use allowlist for internal service access. Implement network segmentation. Require authentication for internal services.

flags.retrieval_method: Multi-stage: IDOR → Blind SQLi → SSRF → Metadata Service

realm_chaining.notes: Final realm - completing Asgard means conquering all of Yggdrasil

exploit_chain.name: IDOR Reconnaissance
exploit_chain.objective: Enumerate employee IDs to find admin email

exploit_chain.name: Blind SQL Injection
exploit_chain.objective: Extract password reset token using blind SQLi
exploit_chain.success_indicator: Obtain valid reset token for admin account

exploit_chain.name: Account Takeover
exploit_chain.objective: Reset admin password and gain admin access

exploit_chain.name: SSRF via CRLF
exploit_chain.objective: Bypass SSRF filters using CRLF injection

learning_objectives: Learn CRLF injection for SSRF bypass

scanner_test_cases.name: Detect blind SQLi in password reset

expected_response.notes: Response timing or errors may indicate SQLi

hints.text: Not every door checks your badge. Enumerate endpoints and object identifiers carefully.
Try reaching other users' resources or admin-only routes directly (IDOR / forced browsing).
Escalate through the broken access control to reach the privileged flag.
